description: A smooth black egg, warm on one face and cold on the other. Every year somebody pays soulstone money for one.
lore: Two tests, and a new cracker has both inside a week. Put the find to the inside of the wrist and count ten: [[lore/the_hard_pieces|a hard piece]] is warm the whole way round, and this is warm on one face only, the other going cold against you as you count. Then set a knife-point to it. A hard piece takes no mark; this takes a grey line. Junk, then — twenty-eight gold, and worth it, because they polish, and a black one on a shelf looks like money.

Which is the whole trouble. The man who works them at the ford sells to people three days woken who have heard the word and never held one, and he has never once said it. He says egg. Clearly, every time, and then waits, and lets the buyer supply the rest. He is quite right that he has not lied. The trade has a word for him anyway.
gm_notes: No creature is bound to this one and none should be — it is a found thing, and the sprite is a plain glossy egg. The two tests are the useful export: any table can now check a stone a player was sold. The ford man is a low, human antagonist for a first hour of play, and the point of him is that he cannot be caught out on a word; the only case against him is what he leaves people to assume, which is the same fraud the whole trade runs on at a larger scale.
